newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE GERMAN FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Programme of matches in the German first division this weekend:

1860 Munich (8) v Borussia Moenchengladbach (10). 1860 are without Abedi Pele who is on international duty for Ghana but the home side, who won this fixture 4-0 last season, have most of their other key players fit. Moenchengladbach are showing good form after a poor start to the season. Playmaker Stefan Effenberg returns after suspension.

Cologne (9) v Duisburg (14). Cologne have not won in their last five games and will be missing defender Karsten Baumann and midfielder Ralf Hauptmann (both suspended). Duisburg have won just three away games all season.

Borussia Dortmund (3) v Bochum (6). With the tight position at the top, Dortmund need to focus on the domestic scene before next week's European Cup semifinal against Manchester United. Midfielder Steffen Freund and defender Rene Schneider return to the squad after injury. Despite their recent shock defeat at home by Moenchengladbach, Dortmund have an excellent record at home. Promoted Bochum will be highly motivated with a UEFA Cup place firmly in their sights.
Fortuna Duesseldorf (15) v St. Pauli (17). Just two points separate the teams in this relegation battle. Fortuna have a poor scoring record at home and have lost their last three games.

Karlsruhe (5) v Schalke (7). This is a tough game for Schalke a few days before next week's UEFA Cup semifinals. Both teams, who are level on points, need a victory to stay in the race for next season's UEFA Cup places.

Werder Bremen (11) v Arminia Bielefeld (13). After struggling earlier in the season, promoted Bielefeld are looking a good bet to stay in the Bundesliga. This is a good opportunity to get points away from home.

Hamburg (12) v Bayern Munich (1). Bayern are struggling with internal squabbling again but should have a strong team to take north. Internationals Thomas Strunz and Mehmet Scholl may return after injury. Hamburg have problems with their defence.

Hansa Rostock (16) v Bayer Leverkusen (2). Both teams have everything to play for with their respective battles against relegation and for the championship. Leverkusen have a good record away from home and this is a good opportunity to pick up points. Hansa have never beaten them at home.

Freiburg (18) v VfB Stuttgart (4). Stuttgart will be without suspended Brazilian striker Giovane Elber but should be strong enough to beat a team who have won just three games at home this season. Freiburg look doomed to drop to the second division next season with just 14 points from 25 games.
